title: KV onboarding preflight & sequence-distribution heuristic audit
creator: Luca Moreno
description:
Goal: Define and validate a deterministic preflight audit that produces per-model KV cache onboarding recommendations based on realistic sequence distributions. This ticket covers the heuristic design, sampling strategy, offline simulation, and gating criteria to publish a model performance profile (KV hit-rate, latency p95, token/sec throughput) into the model catalog.

Background: Recent model rollouts revealed unstable KV warmup behavior for long-context variants; some models exhibit a pronounced tail where KV hit-rate drops >15% for infrequent long-sequence clusters, causing 40–200ms p95 regressions. We need a standardized preflight that: (1) detects such long-tail sensitivity, (2) outputs a pinning/lock recommendation or warmup override, and (3) emits a publishable profile artifact for the model catalog and rollout automation.

Acceptance criteria:
- Sampling strategy defined: how to synthesize and select sequence clusters from production traces and synthetic workloads (including prefix repeats, interleaved short+long sequences).
- Offline simulator implemented that replays sequences against the candidate model + runtime kernel config to estimate KV hit-rate, latency p50/p95, and token throughput.
- Gating thresholds documented (example: KV hit-rate drop >12% vs baseline OR p95 regression >100ms triggers advisory pin + canary required).
- Profile artifact format example (JSON) produced and validated against model-catalog ingestion.
- Runbook for rollout: smoke tests, staged publish windows, rollback criteria, and notification hooks to SRE/PM.

Planned approach:
1) Data collection: sample 10k sequences from recent production traces stratified by session length and user cohort; augment with synthetic long-seq generation (1k sequences per 2k–64k token lengths) to stress tails.
2) Cluster sequences using a lightweight signature (prefix token hash + length bin + entropy) to create representative cluster centroids.
3) Simulate: use the offline runtime simulator to step through request sequences and capture KV hit-rate over time, per-step latency, and cache warmup curves.
4) Metrics and thresholds: compare candidate model profile to baseline model variant; compute delta p50/p95, KV hit-rate AUC over first 1024 tokens, and tail (98th percentile) sequence behavior.
5) Output: a profile document with recommended pin window (if any), warmup override flags, and suggested rollout plan (canary %, duration).

Risks & notes:
- Synthetic sequences may not perfectly mirror correlated user behavior; ensure production sampling remains the primary signal.
- Simulator accuracy depends on kernel selection fidelity; coordinate with runtime infra to ensure kernel parity.
- Publishing profiles can affect many routes; conservative defaults recommended for first rollouts.

Next steps:
- Finalize sampling buckets (Priya) by 2026-03-01.
- Implement simulator hooks (Eng Runtime) and wire metrics exporter by 2026-03-08.
- Run first audit on cand-model-v1 and produce artifact by 2026-03-12.
